name: cbonsai
desc: Console Bonsai is a bonsai tree generator, written in C using ncurses
why: Grows procedural bonsai trees in the terminal; generative and pleasant, though it leans toward pretty output.

brief.what_it_is: cbonsai is a terminal program that grows procedurally generated bonsai trees, written in C with ncurses, per the Homebrew formula description. The GitLab project page I fetched shows only the tagline "grow bonsai trees in your terminal" and the GPL-3.0-or-later license, so I could not confirm its options, inputs, or exact output. The executable is named cbonsai. The scout note describes the output as generative and pleasant to watch.
brief.why_it_exists: The fetched pages give no stated motivation beyond the tagline "grow bonsai trees in your terminal".
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew (the formula's executable is cbonsai). The fetched GitLab pages contained no build, dependency, or first-run instructions beyond what Homebrew handles. Since it uses ncurses, a terminal with ncurses support is needed.
brief.standout: A small, self-contained generative toy: a single C binary that draws a different procedural tree in the terminal each run. The scout note calls it generative and pleasant, and it is pitched as a visual toy rather than a utility.
brief.status: unknown. The project was created May 15, 2020 per the GitLab page. I did not see a last release date, last commit date, or any maintenance note on the pages I could load, so I cannot judge whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: Both GitLab fetches returned only page chrome (title, license, creation date, tagline) and no README body, so the usage details, options, and build notes are unverified. The Homebrew formula description is the only source for the 'C with ncurses' detail. The scout note says it leans toward pretty output rather than practical use. License is GPL-3.0-or-later.
